Zakat on circulating paper currency.

It is well known that dealing in paper instead of gold and silver is a matter that arose after the era of the four Imams and the eras of the codification of Islamic jurisprudence, and it spread only in the eighteenth century CE. For this reason none of the Imams - may Allah have mercy on them - had an opinion on it. Since it came into existence, the scholars of the Muslims have differed in evaluating it and in determining its reality, whether it is bonds (sanadat) representing gold or silver, or trade goods (urud tijara), or currency in itself.

The disagreement on this is well known, although what appears - and Allah the Most High knows best - is that they are documents of guarantee (wathaiq daman) from the authority (al-sultan).

It had previously been mentioned from the Shaykh - may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him - stating his view of them concerning riba, and whether gold and silver may be sold for them on credit (nasi'a) or not.

Whatever theories there are about their reality, they are by the agreement of all considered wealth (mal), and they fall within the generality of the Most High's words: ﴿And in their wealth there is a known right﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 24], since they have become the price of goods and the equivalent of commodities.

Accordingly, zakat on them is obligatory. The nisab in relation to them is reckoned by what gold and silver can be bought with them, in whatever currency they are.

So in Saudi Arabia, for example, one looks at how much twenty mithqals of gold, or two hundred dirhams of silver, can be bought with them; that amount is considered the nisab, and zakat is due on it, namely one quarter of a tenth, exactly the same.

Likewise the sterling pound, the rupee and the dollar; for each of these currencies is a document of guarantee from the authority that issued it, i.e. the state that issued it. Whether it is said that zakat is due on what that document guarantees, or on it in its own form, or on its value as trade goods, they will in no way leave the sphere of circulation and exchange; and the poor man's acquisition of any of them will by them attain what he seeks of food, clothing and whatever benefits he wishes, just as he would attain by the very gold and silver.

In this there is a refutation of those who say: there is no zakat on them, because they are not gold or silver currency. It is not hidden that dropping zakat from them amounts to dropping zakat from the majority of the world, if not from all of it.

Note.

I had previously heard from the Shaykh - may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him - on the subject of zakat on trade goods, regarding the position of the Malikis:

It is a condition that there be found in the hand of the managing merchant, even a dirham, during the year; otherwise zakat on the goods of his trade would not be obligatory for him.

He - may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him - said: If Malik - may Allah have mercy on him - were alive today, he would not have said that; for the whole world today hardly knows anything but these papers, and a single silver dirham may not be found in a person's hand at all. This entails dropping zakat from trade goods, which are the majority of people's wealth today.

Likewise, it is said to whoever does not consider zakat due on paper currency: there follows from his position a grave falsehood, namely the nullification of a pillar of zakat and the depriving of the needy of his known right in the wealth of the rich; and whatever entails falsehood is itself false.

Perhaps with this concise presentation we have set forth the essence of what remains of the topic of zakat, though not in the detailed manner customary from the Shaykh - may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him. We have already said that his detail cannot be matched, and that pursuing particulars in this topic would lengthen the writing; it is, praise be to Allah, expounded in the books of fiqh. We intended only to explain the most important questions and what is preponderant in what has been disputed. And success is from Allah the Most High.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who affirm the Day of Judgment﴾

"Yawm al-Din" (the Day of Judgment) is the Day of Reckoning, as the Shaykh - may Allah the Exalted have mercy on us and on him - had already explained in Surat al-Fatihah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who are, from the punishment of their Lord, fearful﴾

That is: fearful (khā'ifūn), as He, exalted is He, explained by His saying: ﴿And for whoever fears the station of his Lord are two gardens﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 46].

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed we were before, among our people, fearful. So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind"﴾ [At-Tur: 26-27].

Almighty Allah says: "And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, then it is those who are the transgressors" (al-Mu'minun 23:5–7; here 70:29–31).

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, previously discussed this at His saying "Successful are the believers" and what follows it, and in Surat al-Nisa', and he explained that everyone who seeks beyond wives and what the right hand possesses is included in His saying: "then it is those who are the transgressors," especially those who hold the permissibility of temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah), since the woman enjoyed in this way is neither a wife nor a bondwoman owned.

(p-295) A reminder.

It is worth mentioning that no one remains who holds temporary marriage as the doctrine of any group except the Shi'ah, setting aside those who opposed the consensus (ijma') among others. Yet the Shi'ah themselves are almost self-contradictory in their books, for al-Hilli (al-Hulli), one of their imams, states explicitly in the chapter on marriage that a free man and a slave alike may contract a time-limited marriage, which is temporary marriage, with any number of women they wish and without limit. Thus he made this contract like ownership by the right hand, while the woman contracted is free, and this is contradictory.

In the Book of Divorce he said that a woman divorced three times is not made lawful to her former husband unless she marries another husband, in a permanent marriage and not a time-limited one.

Here it is said to them: either you count her second, time-limited marriage as valid, in which case it follows that it makes her lawful to the first husband, for He, exalted is He, said: "until she marries a husband other than him" (al-Baqarah 2:230). If you regard it as a marriage, it follows that she is made lawful to the first husband by it. And if you do not regard it as a marriage, it necessarily follows that you must hold it to be void, which is what was sought.

By this it becomes clear that whoever seeks beyond that, namely beyond wives or what their right hands possess, then they are the transgressors.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants﴾

The explanation of this by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) has already come forward at the beginning of the surah of ﴿Successful indeed are the believers﴾.

And in the sixth issue of the issues of the discussion of: ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman, when they gave judgment concerning the field﴾ [al-Anbiya: 78].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 33 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who are steadfast in their testimonies﴾.

It is recited as "bi-shahadatihim" (in their testimonies) in the plural, and as "bi-shahadatihi" (in their testimony) in the singular. It is said that the singular conveys the sense of the plural, since it is a verbal noun (masdar), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the most hideous of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾ [Luqman: 19]. Here "voice" is used in the singular while meaning voices in general.

It is also said that the singular refers to the testimony of monotheism (tawhid), which they uphold, while the plural refers to the variety of testimonies according to their subject matter. There is no contradiction between the two matters. What supports this is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ [Fussilat: 30].

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: That is, they persevered in that until they died upon it.

The general wording of the verse of testimony supports the second view, since it covers varied testimonies in sales, divorce, writing down debts, and other matters. And Allah knows best.

In this verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Here He stated the upholding of testimony without qualification, and He clarified that their upholding of it is for Allah, as in His saying: ﴿And establish testimony for Allah﴾ [al-Talaq: 2], and His saying: ﴿O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa': 135].

The second issue: His saying, ﴿those who are steadfast in their testimonies﴾, is in the context of praise. Their being excluded from the description of ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 19] indicates by implication that those who do not uphold their testimonies are not exempt from that blameworthy description.

Explicit verses have indicated this implication, among them His saying: ﴿And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 283], and His saying: ﴿And we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, we would then be among the sinful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 106].

Likewise, in the context of praise, in describing the servants of the Most Merciful in His saying: ﴿And those who do not bear false witness﴾ [al-Furqan: 72].

In the hadith there is [a statement] on the gravity of the sin of false testimony. The Prophet (ﷺ) was reclining, then he sat up and said: "Beware, and false testimony! Beware, and false testimony!" He kept repeating it until we said, "I wish he would stop."

* *

A caution.

His saying, ﴿those who are steadfast in their testimonies﴾, conveys upholding testimony in an unrestricted sense. And there came His saying: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282], which restricts upholding testimony to being summoned to it.

In a hadith: "The best of witnesses is the one who brings testimony before being asked for it."

In another hadith, which censures hastening to it: "...and they bear witness before they are asked to." The scholars reconciled the two hadiths by saying: the first applies when the one in whose favour the testimony is due does not know that the witness has such testimony, or when a legal right depends on his testimony, such as in suckling, divorce, and the like. The second applies to the opposite of that.

Ibn Farhun explicitly stated that testimony regarding the rights of Allah is of two kinds. One kind is one in which the prohibition persists, such as marriage and divorce, so one must not abandon it, and abandoning it is a blemish on his probity (adalah). The other kind is one in which the prohibition does not persist, such as adultery and drinking, where abandoning testimony is better, unless one is summoned to give it, based on the hadith of Hazzal in the story of Ma'iz, when he said to him (ﷺ): "Why did you not cover him with your garment?"

The third issue: the occasions of testimony mentioned in the Qur'an, in which upholding it is obligatory, which we set out in summary form.

The first: calling witnesses to a sale, based on His saying: ﴿And call witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

The second: divorce and taking back a wife (rj'ah), based on His saying: ﴿So when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness, and bring to witness two just men from among you﴾ [al-Talaq: 2].

The third: writing down a debt, based on His saying: ﴿Let his guardian dictate with justice, and call upon two witnesses from among your men﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

The fourth: a bequest at death, based on His saying: ﴿O you who believe, the testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest is two just men from among you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 106].

The fifth: handing over an orphan's property to him when he comes of age, based on His saying: ﴿And when you hand over to them their property, then call witnesses over them﴾ [al-Nisa': 6].

The sixth: the carrying out of the hudud (prescribed punishments), based on His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

The seventh: in the Sunnah, the contracting of marriage, based on His saying (ﷺ): "There is no marriage except with a guardian and two just witnesses." All of these are important occasions concerning the rights of Allah and the rights of people, such as the preservation of property, honour, and lineage, and concerning the living and the dead, the orphan and the adult. They are of great concern to the welfare of the community, so they require encouragement to uphold them: ﴿And those who are steadfast in their testimonies﴾, and a warning against concealing them: ﴿And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 283].

And His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 140].

And His saying: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

The fourth issue: His saying, ﴿those who are steadfast in their testimonies﴾, all of its forms are plural. Testimony may come from one person, or from two, or from three, or from four, or from a group.

The summary of this is that testimony, in general terms, as urged upon the witness, takes the following forms in summary: one man; a man and an oath; a man and two women; two men; three men; four men; a group of the believers; a woman; two women; and a group of boys.

The texts have stated these explicitly. As for one witness, He said: ﴿And a witness from her own family testified: "If her shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth"﴾ [Yusuf: 26].

Although he drew attention to the circumstantial evidence in the tearing of the shirt, he was nevertheless a single witness.

The Sunnah includes the testimony of Khuzayma (may Allah be pleased with him), when he testified to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the purchase of the horse from the Bedouin, and the Prophet (ﷺ) treated it as equal to the testimony of two men.

The Sunnah also established the testimony of a physician, a physiognomist (qa'if, one who identifies lineage by physical resemblance), an assessor of crops (kharis), and others like them.

As for the sighting of Ramadan, the Prophet (ﷺ) accepted the testimony of a Bedouin, and he accepted the testimony of Abdullah ibn Umar, whether his acceptance was to rely on it alone or as a precaution for Ramadan.

As for the testimony of one man together with the oath of the claimant, it is based on the hadith of Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decided by a witness and an oath." Ibn Abd al-Barr discussed it at length, and he extended his efforts to authenticate it and to explain its meaning.

According to Malik, and according to one view attributed to Ahmad, the testimony of two women together with the oath of the claimant suffices. The majority disagreed with both of them.

As for the testimony of a man and two women, it is based on His saying: ﴿But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

He, may He be exalted, explained the reason for this in His saying: ﴿So that if one of the two errs, the other can remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

On the basis of this text, the majority rejected the view of Malik and the view attributed to Ahmad, because it reports only four women, and equality in testimony was not established.

As for the testimony of two men, it is based on His saying: ﴿And call upon two witnesses from among your men﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

As for three men, it is based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying concerning the establishing of destitution and hardship: "Until three wise men from his people stand up and say, 'Indeed, so-and-so has been struck by destitution,'" and the hadith continues. This is the hadith of Qabisa in Muslim and Ahmad.

As for four, it applies specifically to establishing adultery. The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, explained this at the beginning of surah al-Nur.

As for a group, it applies to the carrying out of the hudud, based on His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

As for the testimony of a woman, it applies specifically to matters concerning women, as in the hadith of Uqba ibn al-Harith: "A woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'I have nursed them both.' So he said to him (ﷺ), 'Separate from her.' He said, 'How can I separate from her on the word of a woman?' So he said to him, 'How, when it has been said?'" The disagreement has occurred concerning the acceptance of her testimony alone, but the sound view is what we have mentioned above.

As for two women, it applies according to those who do not accept the testimony of a woman, and it was said it applies to the cry of a newborn (istihlal al-sabiy), because it is usual for more than one woman to be present.

As for a group of boys, it applies to their offences against one another, and before they disperse, and no adult has joined them. There is disagreement on this.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, preferred acting upon it in the treatise on the principles of jurisprudence (Usul al-Fiqh), in the section on the transmission of children.

The fifth issue: they agreed that women have no role in testimony concerning the hudud. Rather, it applies to property, or what leads to property, and to matters concerning what is beneath the clothing of women.

There are numerous discussions concerning testimony, set out at length in the books of jurisprudence and the books of judicature, such as Tabsirat al-Hukkam (The Insight of Judges) by Ibn Farhun and others.

Ibn al-Qayyim discussed it at length in al-Turuq al-Hukmiyya, and Ibn Farhun in Tabsirat al-Hukkam, for whoever wishes to refer to them. But of what is indispensable is the conditions for an acceptable witness, all of which revolve around what brings reassurance regarding the truth of the matter testified to, for two fundamental reasons: accuracy of memory (dabt), as in His saying concerning women: ﴿So that if one of the two errs, the other can remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]; and the second is uprightness (adalah) and truthfulness, as in His saying: ﴿If a degenerate comes to you with news, verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6].

Here there is a well-known question: is the default state of Muslims uprightness until their impeachment becomes evident, or the reverse?

The correct view is the first.

The practice was based on this until a man from Iraq came to Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) and said to him: "Pay attention to the people; false testimony has become widespread." Umar said: "Then by vouching for the witnesses and establishing their uprightness."

Ibn Farhun listed eleven ranks of witnesses, and they are:

The first: the witness who is outstanding in uprightness and knowledgeable in what makes testimony valid. His testimony is accepted in everything, and he may impeach others. He is not questioned about how he came to know what he testified to, if he gave it in general terms, and impeachment of him is not accepted except on grounds of enmity.

The second: one outstanding in uprightness but not knowledgeable in what makes testimony valid. His ruling is the same as the first, except that he is questioned about how he came to know what he testified to, if he gave it in general terms.

The third: a witness known for uprightness and knowledgeable in what makes testimony valid. His testimony is accepted except in six situations, on which there is disagreement regarding some of them. They are: giving a certification of another's probity; his testimony for his brother, for his client (mawla), for his close friend, and for his partner in matters other than trade; and when he adds to or subtracts from his testimony. Impeachment of him is accepted on grounds of enmity and otherwise, and he is not questioned about how he came to know what he testified to, if he gave it in general terms.

The fourth: one known for uprightness but not knowledgeable in what makes testimony valid. His ruling is the same, except that he is questioned about how he came to know what he testified to, if he gave it in general terms.

The fifth: a witness known for uprightness who has slandered someone before being punished (hadd). There is disagreement on accepting his testimony. Ibn al-Qasim permitted it, and this is the view of Malik.

The sixth: one in whom uprightness is presumed. His testimony is acceptable without vouching for him in matters arising between travellers on a journey concerning transactions. In other matters, he must be vouched for, because he is someone whose condition is unknown, known only as unknown in condition.

The sound view is that someone like him must be investigated until his situation becomes clear.

The seventh: one in whom neither uprightness nor impeachment is presumed. His testimony is not acceptable in any situation without vouching for him, except that his testimony is treated as similar in some situations according to some scholars, so it requires an oath, requires a surety (hamil), and requires the holding of the object in dispute by the defendant.

The eighth: one in whom impeachment is presumed. His testimony is not acceptable without vouching for him, and his testimony does not constitute a doubt that establishes a ruling.

The Tenth Case: the witness who is known to have an old discrediting (jarh) on record, or whose discrediting the judge knows about. His testimony is not permissible without a commendation (tazkiyah), and a commendation of him is not accepted in absolute terms. It is accepted only from someone who knows of his discrediting, when that person testifies to his repentance from it and his departure from it.

The one convicted of slander (qadhf) has the same status according to the school of Malik, because his commendation is not permissible in absolute terms. It is permissible only with knowledge that adds to the report's reliability.

The Tenth: the witness who persists in the discrediting for which he has been testified against. His testimony is not permissible, and a commendation of him is not accepted, even if he is commended. His commendation is accepted only for what follows, once he repents.

The Eleventh: the false witness (shahid al-zur). His testimony is not valid, even if he repents and his condition becomes good. Abu Zayd narrated from Ibn al-Qasim that his testimony is permissible if he repents and his repentance is known through the improvement of his righteous condition.

He (Ibn al-Qasim) said: "I know of no one who holds this except according to the view of Malik." It was said: "This is a divergence in the statement (of Malik)."

It was also said: "The meaning of Abu Zayd's narration is that he came repentant, confessing on himself the false testimony, before it was discovered against him." This is the more apparent meaning. And God, glory be to Him, knows best. End of quotation.

We have set out these ranks because they cover the types of witnesses in terms of strength and weakness, and what their testimonies are accepted for.

(p-302) Note.

It has been said regarding the separation of witnesses (tafriq al-shuhud) that this applies to adultery specifically. It has also been said that the judge may separate them whenever he sees fit, and that the first to separate them was ʿAli, may God be pleased with him. The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, mentioned the separation of witnesses in the story of Sulayman, which concerns the case of the woman accused of adultery. There is a difference of opinion regarding making a witness take an oath.

The majority say he is not made to swear. Ibn al-Qayyim preferred its permissibility in cases where testimony is accepted out of necessity, such as a single woman and a non-Muslim on a journey. The basis for accepting testimony is the assurance of the witness's truthfulness, and this revolves around two principles:

The first is accuracy (al-dabt), as in God's words: ﴿So that if one of them errs, the other can remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

The second is uprightness (al-ʿadalah), as in God's words: ﴿If a defiant person brings you a report, verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6]. And God knows best.

Testimony has many further discussions, but we have been content with what we have set out.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, discussed the matters of testimony in terms of number and subject in his book al-Turuq al-Hukmiyyah.

Note.

Testimony has a connection with oath in judgment, as seen in the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Two witnesses or his oath."

What, then, is that connection? It is explained by God's words: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say: "God is witness between me and you"﴾ [al-Anʿam: 19]; His words: ﴿Is it not sufficient that your Lord is a witness over all things?﴾ [Fussilat: 53]; His words: ﴿And We were witnesses to their judgment﴾ [al-Anbiya: 78]; and His words: ﴿He knows best what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8]. And similar verses. This is because He, exalted is He, is the witness and is aware of the conditions of the servants; nothing is hidden from Him. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. So when the claimant lacks a witness, he swears together with the witness, as if he were saying: "I call upon God, who knows from me the truth of my claim."

Likewise the defendant: when the claimant is unable to produce evidence and the claim is directed at him, he says, as the Malikis say: "I have evidence, and the testimony that what he claims against me is not established, and that is the best of witnesses."

Who is greater in testimony than that which the claimant could not produce? That is calling God, exalted is He, as witness, so he swears to the clearing of his obligation from what was claimed against him.

Note.

From here the reality of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying is known: "Whoever swears by other than God has committed shirk." That is, because the one who swears makes the thing sworn by stand in the place of witnesses who saw or heard. A created being, when absent, neither sees nor hears; so when one swears by him, he has ascribed to him the attributes of one who sees and hears, while the reality is otherwise. From another angle, the one who swears by God and the one who requires the oath by God both know that God is able to take vengeance on the perpetrator of a deliberate false oath, whereas other than God, when sworn by, has no power and cannot do anything of that kind. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 36:

Allah's words: ﴿So what is wrong with those who disbelieve, rushing towards you,﴾ ﴿from the right and from the left, in groups?﴾

"Muhti'in" (مُهْطِعِينَ): meaning hastening, fleeing away. "'Izin" (عِزِينَ) is the plural of "'izah" (عِزَةٌ), which means a group. The meaning is: what is the matter with those disbelievers who turn away from you, scattering in different directions? Upon this is the verse of al-Kumayt:

"And we, and Jandal, a rebellious host, left the battalions of Jandal scattered in groups (ʿizīn)."

Likewise here, they are scattered away from him ﷺ in groups from every direction, from the right and from the left. Desires have scattered them and confusion has seized them, as in His saying: ﴿Then what is wrong with them that they turn away from the Reminder?﴾ ﴿As if they were startled donkeys﴾ ﴿fleeing from a lion﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 49–51].

Ibn Kathir, quoting Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) concerning the people of desires, said: they oppose the Book, they disagree among themselves, and they agree in opposing the Book.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We created them from that which they know﴾

The general term "that which they know" (ما يَعْلَمُونَ) is made explicit by the relative pronoun "mimma" (from what). Allah, exalted is He, has clarified it in several stages: first from dust, then from a drop of semen (nutfah). The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained this in more than one place. The most explicit text on this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did We not create you from a despicable fluid?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20], and His saying: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq: 5-7]. That is, the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman mix together, as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worthy of mention? Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture (nutfah amshaj)﴾ [al-Insan: 1-2].

As for His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, We created them from that which they know﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 39], it is not merely for the purpose of informing, because they already know it, and one who knows has no need of being informed. Rather, what is intended is the necessary implication of the statement (lazim al-khabar), which is making them understand that He who created them from this thing which they know is able to restore them, resurrect them, and recompense them. This is as in Surat al-Dahr: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture, to test him, and We made him hearing and seeing﴾ [al-Insan: 2]. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Insan: 3]. Then He explained the final destination: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing fire﴾, ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 4-5].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I swear not by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So I swear not﴾: its apparent meaning is negation, while the actual situation is that He has sworn, as evidenced by the answer of the oath that follows it: ﴿Indeed, We are able﴾ ﴿to replace them with better than them﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 40-41]. The scholars have a great deal of discussion regarding the coming of this "la" (negative particle). The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, explained it in detail in his work on removing the appearance of inconsistency in Surah al-Balad, and it will be printed, God willing, at the end of this supplement.

As for His saying: ﴿by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 40], He is Allah, exalted is He, the Lord and Sovereign of everything. He has explicitly mentioned its counterpart in Surah al-Rahman: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 17-18].

Here "al-mashariq" (the easts) is given in the plural, while in al-Rahman it is given in the dual, and in His saying ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west﴾ [al-Baqarah: 115] it is given in the singular. The plural refers to the risings of the sun over the course of the year, for each day has a rising point (p-305), as Ibn 'Abbas said; the dual refers to the rising points of the sun and the moon; and the singular refers to the direction. This will also come up in the discussion of removing the appearance of inconsistency.

The Exalted said: ﴿On the Day they emerge from the graves swiftly﴾

Here He explains the condition of emerging from the graves (al-ajdath), which are the tombs: that they come forth swiftly (sira'an). In another place He explains that they come forth scattered (mubatharin) here and there, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When what is in the graves is scattered﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 9], and in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿On that Day people will issue forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 70, verse 44:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿With eyes downcast, humiliation will cover them﴾, is a second state. He had gathered the states in the surah "The Hour has drawn near" (Surah al-Qamar), in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when the caller calls to a terrible thing, [with] eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were scattered locusts, hastening toward the caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ [al-Qamar: 6-8]. We ask Allah, the Exalted, for safety and well-being.

At the close of this noble surah, this description and severe warning are a confirmation of the saying that their question at its beginning, "with a punishment that will surely occur," was only mockery and disbelief in its occurrence. So after presenting the surah, Allah, the Exalted, made clear to them the final outcome of what they will face, so that they would take their precaution and return to their Lord. Thus the end of the surah is linked to its beginning.
